questions.question: How many hexadecimal digits are needed to display a full Ethernet MAC address without separators?
questions.explanation: A MAC has 48 bits, and each hexadecimal digit represents four.

option_explanations.A: Eight hex digits encode only 32 bits.
option_explanations.B: Sixteen digits encode 64 bits, more than a standard 48-bit MAC.
option_explanations.D: A MAC has 48 bits, and each hexadecimal digit represents four.

questions.question: Which Ethernet field lets a receiver detect a corrupted frame?
questions.explanation: The FCS contains a CRC computed over the frame contents.

option_explanations.B: The source MAC identifies the link-layer origin.
option_explanations.C: The preamble helps the receiver synchronize before the frame.
option_explanations.D: The FCS contains a CRC computed over the frame contents.

questions.question: Which colon-separated address equals IOS notation 001a.2b03.04c5?
questions.explanation: Keep the original digit order and regroup the digits into pairs.

option_explanations.A: 40 reverses the nibbles in the fifth octet, which should be 04.
option_explanations.B: 30 reverses the nibbles in the fourth octet, which should be 03.
option_explanations.C: Keep the original digit order and regroup the digits into pairs.
option_explanations.D: b2 reverses the nibbles in the third octet, which should be 2b.

questions.question: For a universally administered address assigned using a traditional 24-bit OUI, which part identifies the registered organization?
questions.explanation: A traditional OUI is the leading 24 bits. Later bits distinguish assigned interfaces.

option_explanations.A: The final two octets are part of the interface portion.
option_explanations.B: Under a 24-bit OUI, the final three octets distinguish individual assignments.
option_explanations.C: Two octets provide only 16 of the 24 OUI bits.
option_explanations.D: A traditional OUI is the leading 24 bits. Later bits distinguish assigned interfaces.

questions.question: An analyst sees EtherType 0x0800 in an untagged Ethernet II frame. What follows the EtherType field?
questions.explanation: EtherType 0x0800 identifies IPv4. ARP uses 0x0806 and IPv6 uses 0x86DD.

option_explanations.A: EtherType 0x0800 identifies IPv4. ARP uses 0x0806 and IPv6 uses 0x86DD.
option_explanations.D: The FCS appears at the end of the frame after the payload.

questions.question: The first six bytes after the Ethernet start frame delimiter are 00 1a 2b 00 00 01. What do they identify?
questions.explanation: In an Ethernet II frame the destination MAC comes first, followed by the source MAC and EtherType.

option_explanations.A: In an Ethernet II frame the destination MAC comes first, followed by the source MAC and EtherType.
option_explanations.B: The source IP is inside the encapsulated IP packet when one is present.
option_explanations.C: The second six bytes carry the Ethernet source MAC.
option_explanations.D: EtherType or length comes after both MAC fields.

questions.question: A router receives an Ethernet frame and routes its IP packet back out a different Ethernet interface. Which MAC appears as the source of the new frame?

options.A: The router on its ingress interface
options.B: The router out of its egress interface

questions.explanation: The router builds a new Layer 2 frame on the outgoing link and uses that interface as the source.

option_explanations.A: The ingress MAC belongs to the old link and is not the outgoing source.
option_explanations.B: The router builds a new Layer 2 frame on the outgoing link and uses that interface as the source.
option_explanations.C: Routing discards the incoming link-layer header and creates a new one.
option_explanations.D: A destination host does not supply the source MAC of the router's outbound frame.

questions.question: An interface uses a locally administered MAC. Why can an OUI lookup fail to identify its hardware vendor?

options.A: The Ethernet frame uses only the last 24 bits of that address
options.B: Switches replace the OUI with the incoming port number
options.C: The prefix is software-selected and need not represent its vendor's assignment
options.D: A universally administered MAC omits its organization bits

questions.explanation: Local administration allows an address to be set independently of the manufacturer's allocation.

option_explanations.A: The frame carries the full 48-bit MAC address.
option_explanations.B: Ordinary switches learn MAC addresses without rewriting the vendor prefix.
option_explanations.C: Local administration allows an address to be set independently of the manufacturer's allocation.
option_explanations.D: A traditional universally administered assignment includes the assigned organization prefix.

questions.question: A receiver discards a frame after an FCS mismatch. Which mechanism can recover the missing application bytes when the payload used TCP?

options.A: An ICMP message that recreates the original frame
options.B: ARP retransmission of the original byte stream
options.C: An Ethernet FCS correction at the receiver

questions.explanation: Ethernet FCS detects errors. A higher-layer reliable protocol such as TCP can resend lost data.

option_explanations.A: ICMP does not reconstruct a dropped Ethernet frame or retransmit TCP application bytes.
option_explanations.B: ARP resolves neighbor addresses, not lost application data.
option_explanations.C: The FCS detects corruption but does not correct it.
option_explanations.D: Ethernet FCS detects errors. A higher-layer reliable protocol such as TCP can resend lost data.

questions.question: A frame arrives with destination 00:1a:2b:03:04:c5 and type 0x0806. Which field does an ordinary Layer 2 switch consult to select the egress port for a known unicast?

options.B: The first IPv4 address carried by ARP

questions.explanation: The MAC forwarding table uses the destination MAC in the VLAN. EtherType identifies the payload instead.

option_explanations.A: 0x0806 identifies an ARP payload, not an egress port.
option_explanations.B: Ordinary Ethernet unicast forwarding uses Layer 2 addresses, not addresses inside ARP.
option_explanations.C: The FCS validates the frame rather than selecting the output port.
option_explanations.D: The MAC forwarding table uses the destination MAC in the VLAN. EtherType identifies the payload instead.
